title: Machine learning and ab initio screening predict 60 stable two-dimensional ferroelectric bimetal phosphates
summary: A data-driven machine-learning search combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations screened 2,964 two-dimensional bimetal phosphates and identified 60 computationally stable structures with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: 16 predicted ferroelectric metals and 44 predicted ferroelectric semiconductors, including seven predicted multiferroics. The calculations analyze how bimetal displacement can support polarization alongside metallicity. These are theoretical candidates and proposed physical explanations, not experimentally synthesized or measured phases.
ai_technology: Data-driven machine-learning screening with orbital-based descriptors, combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and collaborators

evidence.tested: A data-driven machine-learning search combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations screened 2,964 two-dimensional bimetal phosphates and identified 60 computationally stable structures with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: 16 predicted ferroelectric metals and 44 predicted ferroelectric semiconductors, including seven predicted multiferroics.
evidence.unknown: The 60 phases and their stability and ferroelectric properties are computational predictions from high-throughput ab initio calculations. The paper does not report experimental synthesis or measurement of these predicted structures; practical stability and device behavior remain unverified.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning with newly developed electronic-orbital descriptors enabled systematic screening of 2,964 candidate 2D bimetal phosphates; first-principles calculations evaluated stability, polarization, and electronic structure for the reported candidate family.
